subject: Bayesian Analysis for Penalized Spline Regression

messages.author: fecbe3dc811bed89
messages.subject: Bayesian Analysis for Penalized Spline Regression
parts:
Dear NIMBLE authors,

I was trying to replicate a very basic analysis of a penalized spline regression, described in a paper titled "Bayesian Analysis for Penalized Spline Regression Using WinBUGS" (see  https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v014i14). As it works by WinBUGS, I wonder if NIMBLE can replicate the results therein. I obtained the data from the `SemiPar` package, though the data seem a bit different from the scatter plot.

I have attached the NIMBLE syntax that tries to replicate the age-income example. However, the results are quite different from Table 1. I also compared my NIMBLE syntax with the WinBUGS syntax in the paper but didn't find any marked difference.

I am not sure that the difference results from the NIMBLE or anything I missed. Hope you could help to have a look at this issue.

Thank you for the excellent NIMBLE package!

Best wishes,
Keith

messages.author: fecbe3dc811bed89
messages.subject: Re: Bayesian Analysis for Penalized Spline Regression
parts:
I notice that the paper gave initial values of `b` with all zeros, so I tried it again. I ran longer and multiple chains, and plotted the trace (see the attached R code). The `beta` parameters seem to be difficult to converge, which is odd. WinBUGS seems to give a similar phenomenon to NIMBLE. Although now NIMBLE gave results closer to the paper. It may mean that this spline regression model is very sensitive to initial values and unstable.

messages.subject: Re: Bayesian Analysis for Penalized Spline Regression
parts:
Oh, the problem with the  betas is that the intercept and the slope are trading off. Trying subtracting the mean of 'covariate' off from 'covariate'. That's the standard approach for removing the negative correlation between slope and intercept in regression contexts. 

-Chris
